newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Implats says refinery workers on strike.
newsitem.headline: Implats says refinery workers on strike.

text.p: Impala Platinum Ltd said on Tuesday that workers at its refineries had gone on strike from August 4 over pay.

It said that over the last 24 hours, attempts had been made by a faction of the striking employees to disrupt operations, but that a range of plans had been put in place to minimise any impact on metal output.
"Production is anticipated to run at close to or at normal levels at least in the short-to-medium term," the company said in a statement.

The strike by members of the National Union of Mineworkers (NUM) had been planned for August 1, but was put on hold pending a meeting of the Commission for Conciliation, Mediation and Arbitration over the wage dispute.
Management's last wage offer was a 10.7 percent increase, the NUM's last offer was 19.2 percent.
Implats produced 499,000 ounces of refined platinum in the six months to end-December 1996.
